_comment: Player contract: bump whenever pack.ts starts emitting something an older player/game.js cannot read. The player build stamps this into public/player/build.json; publishClient refuses to publish when the two disagree, and the player refuses to boot a game.bin from a newer packer. v1 = every bundle built before the guard existed (no build.json at all) -- notably the 2026-07-22 bundle that predates terrain heightChunk/splatChunk and animation-field playback. v3 adds tilemap cell chunks: a v2 player ignores `chunk` on a tile chunk and would render an empty map with nothing logged, which is exactly the silent failure this number exists to prevent. v4 moves UI out of `scenes[].ui` and into UI nodes in the scene tree: a v3 player has no UI node classes, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse and the game renders no HUD at all, silently -- again exactly what this number exists to catch. v5 moves SHARED animation clips out of the serialized nodes and into a game-level `animations` array (with `modelAnimations` saying which model plays which), retargeted onto each character at load: a v4 player never runs that step, so every character that uses a shared clip stands in its bind pose with nothing logged. v6 moves a skinned model's per-vertex bone data (`jointIndices`/`jointWeights`) out of the manifest JSON and into blob chunks, because Model.serialize now writes those as typed arrays and a typed array stringifies as {"0":..} rather than an array: a v5 player finds neither the chunk it does not know about nor a readable array, so every skinned character loads with no bone weights and collapses to the origin -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v7 adds NavMeshNode: a v6 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, scene.navMeshes comes back empty, and every controller on a `path` or `patrol` goal falls back to walking in a straight line into the geometry it was supposed to route around -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v8 adds DecalNode: a v7 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, each decal loads as a plain Node with its `decal` payload dropped, and every scorch mark, painted road line and area-of-effect ring is missing from the published game -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v9 replaces the terrain's 4-layer normalized splat with a layer STACK: a base landscape material plus ordered paint layers, each with a mask channel in a `masksChunk`, and slot rules evaluated in the shader. A v8 player knows `splatChunk` and four `layers`, finds neither, and draws every landscape in its base colour with no painted roads, no rules and no foliage rules bound to a layer -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v10 adds controller LAYERS, action SLOTS, pose states, clip-owned events and skeleton SOCKETS (`stateMachine.layers/slots`, `state.pose`, `animation.events`, `skin.sockets`, node `socketAttachment`): a v9 player ignores all of them, so an upper-body layer never plays, a held weapon stays where it was placed instead of following the hand, and footstep events on clips never fire -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v11 adds ParticleSystemNode and ForceFieldNode: a v10 player has no such classes, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, each loads as a plain Node with its `particleSystem` / `forceField` payload dropped, and every fire, spark, smoke plume and wind zone is missing from the published game -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch. v12 adds WaterVolumeNode: a v11 player has no such class, so parseNodeJson falls through to Node.parse, the `waterVolume` payload is dropped, and nothing floats -- crates and logs sink through the pond and the surface never ripples -- silently, which is what this number exists to catch.
